capabilities: Manage tickets as plain notes on kanban boards driven by frontmatter
Dispatch coding agents to repositories with per-card chip commands
Plan releases with drag-and-drop grouping, progress and forecasts
Run meetings from board agendas and fold transcripts into tickets
Track refinement and manual-test state with per-card badges
extras: Desktop only — chips and automations spawn local processes, so there is no mobile version; boards still render without an agent CLI or Node installed. Full documentation lives in separate pages (Overview, Wiki structure, Page types, Workflow skills, Installation & configuration); setup can be delegated to a coding agent via a bundled skill, and feedback is collected through GitHub Discussions.
intentEvidence: an agent-friendly wiki (à la Karpathy's LLM wiki pattern)
motivation: The author says coding agents now ship faster than teams can decide, so the bottleneck is refinement, agreement and review, and an agent-friendly wiki should become the cockpit for that human side.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to run a team ticket workflow that turns notes into a board and sends coding agents at the work from a card.

relations.evidence: every card can dispatch a coding agent — Claude Code, Codex, any CLI
so Claude Code and Codex run the same process instead of two copies
The agent posts a ticket's open questions into your team chat (Slack via MCP)
a NoteTaker transcript (e.g. Google Gemini) becomes an interpreted report
an agent-friendly wiki (à la Karpathy's LLM wiki pattern)

requires.name: coding agent CLI (Claude Code, Codex, or any CLI) on PATH

summary: Kanban board over note frontmatter that dispatches coding agents like Claude Code to tickets and runs team refinement, releases and meetings.
